text:
Maya Chen: rough idea 1: reduce noise in run history by hiding full tool payloads behind a compact "preview chip" that reveals on click/enter. dropping a quick Figma frame: https://www.figma.com/file/fake/preview
Diego Ramos: I like. question: should the preview show pretty-printed JSON or a one-line summary + key/value badges?
Riley Thompson: one-line summary + badges for keys we detect (e.g., id, status, url). show a "raw" toggle inside the inspector for power users.
Maya Chen: agrees. keeps density high for quick scans. UX note: we need an obvious affordance for keyboard users. thumbs down on hover-only reveals.
Accessibility-bot: recommendation: make the chip focusable (tabindex=0), expose aria-expanded, and include aria-controls referencing the inspector region id. also ensure escape closes inspector and focus returns to chip.
Diego Ramos: nice. copy decision: label the chip "Tool output" vs "Output preview"? product leaning toward "Preview" to avoid jargon.
Riley Thompson: "Output preview" is friendly. inside inspector header include a tiny label "Schema" if we detect a schema field.
Maya Chen: another item: error state behavior. when a tool returns error, surface a short inline error banner in the row and push a subtle pulse on the chip. aria-live should announce "Tool failure".+details.
Accessibility-bot: add aria-live="assertive" for error updates and make the banner dismissible via keyboard. also ensure contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 for banner text on bg.
Diego Ramos: visual polish: let's soften the chip color to a charcoal outline (#374151) and white bg. current blue draws too much attention.
Riley Thompson: agree. keep the count badge (e.g., "3 calls") but make it a smaller muted capsule.
Maya Chen: micro-interaction ask: animate the inspector open with a fade+translateY 80ms, don't move the rest of the list (overlay panel). keeps context.
Diego Ramos: implemented a quick prototype in the playground branch. keyboard nav works but screen-reader reads the whole JSON when inspector opens. we want a summary first, then a "Read full JSON" button.
Accessibility-bot: guidance: on open, focus inspector header and announce a short summary using a visually-hidden element then allow user to expand full JSON with a button that toggles aria-expanded.
Riley Thompson: small copy tweak: inspector header text "Output preview" then a secondary line: "Detected: order_id, total" if keys found. short and scannable.
Maya Chen: agree. PR checklist: 1) focusable chip 2) aria attributes 3) error aria-live 4) soft chip colors 5) inspector overlay 6) raw JSON toggle + read button 7) animation 8) tests for keyboard flow
UI-bot: deploy-preview: https://staging.redwood.ai/preview/5501 (keyboard flows wired)
Diego Ramos: opened PR 8010: https://github.com/redwood-inference/playground/pull/8010 will add tests + copy updates.
Riley Thompson: I'll add a short a11y test in cypress for focus return on escape.
Maya Chen: thanks all. can we land copy language in the PR before design review? I want to run a short participant test with 3 engineers to verify discoverability.
Diego Ramos: yeah I'll lock copy now and add to PR description.
Accessibility-bot: reminder: include keyboard-only screenshots in the PR and a short screen-reader narration sample.
Maya Chen: perfect. scheduling review for Thursday 10am.
